entropy.definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system

alpha.definition: Fine-structure constant or first Greek letter.

beta.definition: Beta function: RG flow of a coupling with energy scale.

evolve.definition: To change in time according to a dynamical law.

crystal.definition: Periodic arrangement of atoms with long-range order.

curvature.definition: Local measure of departure from flatness.

eigenvalue.definition: Scalar associated with an eigenfunction by a linear operator.

field.definition: A function assigning a value to every point of spacetime.

magnitude.definition: Euclidean length (L2 norm) of a vector.

tensor.definition: Multilinear geometric object transforming under coordinate changes.

trace.definition: Sum of diagonal elements of a matrix.

variance.definition: Second central moment of a probability distribution.

integral.definition: Antiderivative or sum over a continuum.

manifold.definition: Topological space locally homeomorphic to Euclidean space.

scaling.definition: How a quantity transforms under a rescaling of length.

state.definition: A vector in a Hilbert space describing a quantum system.

norm.definition: Function assigning a length to a vector.

operator.definition: Linear map acting on a Hilbert space.

vertex.definition: Interaction node in a Feynman diagram.

partition.definition: Sum over states weighted by Boltzmann factors.

derive.definition: To obtain a result from prior premises.

scale.definition: To change under a rescaling of length or energy.

vector.definition: Element of a vector space with magnitude and direction.

gluon.definition: Gauge boson of QCD mediating the strong interaction.

dimension.definition: Number of independent directions or scaling exponent.

hamiltonian.definition: Operator generating time evolution of a quantum system.

lagrangian.definition: Functional whose stationary points give the equations of motion.

energy.definition: Conserved quantity associated with time-translation symmetry.

coupling.definition: Strength parameter of an interaction term in a Lagrangian.

metric.definition: Bilinear form measuring distances on a manifold.

anomaly.definition: Quantum violation of a classical symmetry.

dispersion.definition: Spread of a distribution; or k-omega relation of a wave.

number.definition: A scalar quantity counting elements of a set.

projector.definition: Idempotent Hermitian operator with eigenvalues 0 and 1.

propagator.definition: Two-point Green's function of a quantum field.

renormalization.definition: Procedure absorbing UV divergences into redefined couplings.

regularization.definition: Method for assigning meaning to divergent integrals.

regulator.definition: Auxiliary parameter introduced to tame divergences.

convection.definition: Heat transport by bulk fluid motion.

instability.definition: Tendency of a state to grow perturbations exponentially.

hubbard.definition: Pertaining to on-site repulsion in lattice fermion models.

tunneling.definition: Quantum hopping of a particle between sites.

interaction.definition: Term in the Hamiltonian connecting two or more degrees of freedom.

brane.definition: Extended object on which open strings or EOW boundaries can end.

ads.definition: Anti-de Sitter spacetime: maximally symmetric negative curvature.

holographic.definition: Realising a lower-dim QFT as a higher-dim gravitational dual.

weyl.definition: Pertaining to local rescaling symmetry of the metric.

chern.definition: Pertaining to Chern number / Chern class.

hadron.definition: Composite particle bound by the strong force.

strong.definition: Pertaining to the strong nuclear interaction or to a large coupling regime.

weak.definition: Pertaining to the weak nuclear interaction or to a small coupling regime.

constant.definition: A quantity whose value does not change under the symmetry considered.

phase.definition: Complex argument or thermodynamic regime of a system.

loop.definition: Closed propagator line in a Feynman diagram.

divergence.definition: Behavior of an integral that grows without bound.

function.definition: Map from one set to another.

functional.definition: Map from a function space to numbers.

derivative.definition: Rate of change of a function with respect to a variable.

geodesic.definition: Locally length-minimizing curve on a manifold.

torsion.definition: Antisymmetric part of an affine connection.

tetrad.definition: Orthonormal frame field on a Lorentzian manifold.

pion.definition: Lightest meson; pseudoscalar bound state of u, d quarks.

diagram.definition: Graphical representation of a perturbative contribution.

casimir.definition: Quadratic invariant of a Lie algebra; or the zero-point energy effect.

dimensional regularization.definition: Continuation of integrals to d = 4 - 2*epsilon dimensions to regulate divergences.

sail diagram.definition: One-loop diagram contributing to LaMET matching with a 'sail' topology.

lamet.definition: Large-Momentum Effective Theory for parton distributions.

matching kernel.definition: Perturbative coefficient linking quasi- and light-cone distributions.

dglap.definition: Evolution equation governing scale dependence of parton distributions.

photopion.definition: Photon-pion production process; central to astrophysical cascades.

synchrotron.definition: Radiation emitted by relativistic charged particles in magnetic fields.

beta function.definition: RG-flow equation d(g)/d(ln mu) encoding scale dependence of a coupling.

weyl anomaly.definition: Quantum violation of Weyl invariance encoded in the trace of T_munu.

path integral.definition: Sum over all field histories weighted by exp(iS/hbar).

hatsugai-kohmoto.definition: HK model: exactly-solvable variant of Hubbard with all-to-all interaction.

parafermion.definition: Z_N generalization of Majorana zero modes.

braiding.definition: Topological operation of exchanging anyons along worldlines.

fusion.definition: Combining two anyons to give a definite anyon type.

verlinde.definition: Pertaining to Verlinde lines and their fusion algebra.

verlinde line.definition: Topological line operator in a 2D CFT.

moore-read.definition: Non-Abelian fractional quantum Hall state at nu=1/2.

filling.definition: Average occupation of a lattice site or Landau level.

hopping.definition: Nearest-neighbor kinetic term in a tight-binding model.

mott.definition: Insulating phase driven by strong interactions at half-filling.

berry.definition: Pertaining to Berry phase / Berry curvature / Berry connection.

chern number.definition: Integer topological invariant of a band Bloch bundle.

wannier.definition: Maximally localized orbital basis derived from Bloch states.

brillouin.definition: First Brillouin zone: primitive cell of reciprocal lattice.

quantum metric.definition: Real symmetric part of the quantum geometric tensor on a band.

fermi liquid.definition: Phase of weakly interacting fermions with long-lived quasiparticles.

quasiparticle.definition: Long-lived excitation of an interacting system.

spin squeezing.definition: Redistribution of quantum uncertainty among collective spin components.

dephasing.definition: Loss of off-diagonal coherence without population change.

dissipation.definition: Energy loss to environmental degrees of freedom.

lindblad.definition: Pertaining to trace-preserving completely-positive Markovian dynamics.

dissipator.definition: Non-Hamiltonian generator of an open-system master equation.

kraus.definition: Pertaining to operator-sum representation of quantum channels.

kraus operator.definition: Operator in the sum representation of a quantum channel.

squeezed state.definition: Gaussian state with sub-shot-noise variance in one quadrature.

coherent state.definition: Eigenstate of the photon annihilation operator; minimum-uncertainty state.

holevo.definition: Upper bound on accessible classical information from a quantum ensemble.

holevo information.definition: Mutual information bound for classical-quantum ensembles.

matrix product.definition: Compact representation of 1D quantum states as tensor networks.

bond dimension.definition: Auxiliary index size controlling MPS entanglement capacity.

pauli.definition: Pertaining to the Pauli sigma matrices generating SU(2).

einstein-hilbert.definition: Standard gravitational action integral of sqrt(-g)*R.

palatini.definition: First-order formulation treating metric and connection independently.

chern-simons.definition: Topological gauge action defined via the CS 3-form.

qft.definition: Quantum field theory: framework combining QM and special relativity.

cavity.definition: Bounded electromagnetic region supporting discrete modes.

tweezer.definition: Tightly focused laser beam trapping a particle by gradient force.

polarizability.definition: Linear response of dipole moment to applied electric field.

rayleigh range.definition: Axial distance over which a Gaussian beam waist doubles in area.

opa.definition: Optical parametric amplifier producing squeezed/entangled light.

photocurrent.definition: Detector current produced by an incident optical field.

oam.definition: Orbital angular momentum of a structured optical field.

helicity.definition: Projection of spin along the direction of motion.

rayleigh.definition: Pertaining to Lord Rayleigh; in hydrodynamics the Ra number.

rayleigh number.definition: Dimensionless ratio controlling onset of convection.

prandtl.definition: Ratio of momentum diffusivity to thermal diffusivity.

darcy.definition: Empirical law for slow flow in porous media.

eigenfunction.definition: Function on which a linear operator acts as a scalar multiple.

growth rate.definition: Exponential rate of size or population increase.

gamma distribution.definition: Continuous distribution parameterised by shape and rate.

waiting time.definition: Random duration between two events of a stochastic process.

autocatalytic.definition: Of a reaction in which a product catalyzes its own production.

homeostasis.definition: Stable maintenance of internal state under perturbation.

expectation value.definition: Mean of an observable in a quantum state.

excited state.definition: Eigenstate of higher energy than the ground state.

density matrix.definition: Positive trace-1 operator describing a mixed quantum state.

interact.definition: To couple to another degree of freedom.

squeeze.definition: To reduce uncertainty in one variable at the cost of its conjugate.

dissipate.definition: To lose energy or coherence to an environment.

renormalize.definition: To absorb divergences into redefined parameters.

regularize.definition: To assign finite meaning to a divergent expression.

braid.definition: To interchange worldlines of anyons or zero-modes.

dot product.definition: Scalar product of two vectors: a.b = sum(a_i * b_i).

perturbative.definition: Expanded as a power series in a small coupling.

nonperturbative.definition: Containing contributions invisible to any finite-order expansion.

free.definition: Non-interacting (in field theory) or unconstrained (in mechanics).

on-shell.definition: Satisfying the classical equations of motion.

off-shell.definition: Not satisfying the classical equations of motion.

dual_to.definition: Binary relation indicating an equivalence under a duality map.

golden ratio.definition: The golden ratio (φ) is approximately 1.61803398874989. It appears throughout nature and mathematics.

zero.definition: Zero (0) is the additive identity. It represents nothing or the absence of quantity.

pi.definition: Pi (π) is approximately 3.14159265358979. It is the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.

logic.definition: Logic is the study of valid reasoning and argumentation.

hydrogen.definition: Hydrogen (H) is element 1, the lightest element. Atomic number 1. Most abundant element in the universe.

helium.definition: Helium (He) is element 2. It is the second lightest element and is inert.

carbon.definition: Carbon (C) is element 6. It is the basis of organic chemistry and all known life.

nitrogen.definition: Nitrogen (N) is element 7. It makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.

oxygen.definition: Oxygen (O) is element 8. Makes up 21% of Earth's atmosphere. Essential for respiration.

iron.definition: Iron (Fe) is element 26. It is the most common element on Earth by mass.

copper.definition: Copper (Cu) is element 29. It is widely used in electrical wiring.

silver.definition: Silver (Ag) is element 47. It has the highest electrical conductivity of any element.

gold.definition: Gold (Au) is element 79. A precious metal. Atomic number 79.

mercury.definition: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, orbiting at about 58 million km. It is the smallest planet.

water.definition: Water (H₂O) is a molecule of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. Chemical formula: H2O.

one.definition: One (1) is the multiplicative identity. Any number multiplied by 1 remains unchanged.

speed of light.definition: The speed of light in vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 metres per second (c ≈ 3×10⁸ m/s).

planck constant.definition: Planck's constant (h) is approximately 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ joule-seconds. It relates photon energy to frequency: E = hf.

gravitational constant.definition: The gravitational constant (G) is approximately 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N⋅m²/kg². It appears in Newton's law of universal gravitation.

boltzmann constant.definition: The Boltzmann constant (k_B) is approximately 1.381 × 10⁻²³ J/K. It relates temperature to energy.

elementary charge.definition: The elementary charge (e) is approximately 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ coulombs. It is the charge of a single proton.

avogadro number.definition: Avogadro's number (N_A) is approximately 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹. It defines the number of particles in one mole.

euler number.definition: Euler's number (e) is approximately 2.71828182845904. It is the base of natural logarithms.

fine structure constant.definition: The fine structure constant (α) is approximately 1/137.036. It characterizes the strength of electromagnetic interaction.

earth.definition: Earth is the third planet from the Sun, with a diameter of about 12,742 km.

sun.definition: The Sun is a G-type main-sequence star at the center of our solar system.

moon.definition: The Moon is Earth only natural satellite, with a diameter of about 3,474 km.

venus.definition: Venus is the second planet from the Sun. It has a thick toxic atmosphere and is the hottest planet in our solar system.

mars.definition: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun. It has a thin atmosphere and is known as the Red Planet.

jupiter.definition: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and the largest in our solar system. It has a Great Red Spot.

saturn.definition: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun, famous for its prominent ring system.

uranus.definition: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun. It rotates on its side.

neptune.definition: Neptune is the eighth and farthest planet from the Sun.

dna.definition: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) carries genetic instructions. It has a double helix structure of nucleotide base pairs.

rna.definition: RNA (ribonucleic acid) is a molecule similar to DNA. It plays key roles in protein synthesis.

cell.definition: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms.

mitochondria.definition: Mitochondria are organelles that generate most of a cell's ATP energy. They have their own DNA.

photosynthesis.definition: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants convert light energy, water, and CO₂ into glucose and oxygen.

evolution.definition: Evolution is the change in species over generations through natural selection, mutation, and genetic drift.

ecosystem.definition: An ecosystem is a community of living organisms interacting with their physical environment.

pythagorean theorem.definition: The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle, a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse.

prime number.definition: A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.

fibonacci sequence.definition: The Fibonacci sequence starts 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ... where each number is the sum of the two preceding ones.

imaginary number.definition: The imaginary unit i is defined as √(-1). Complex numbers have the form a + bi.

infinity.definition: Infinity (∞) is not a number but a concept representing something without bound or end.

internet.definition: The Internet is a global network of interconnected computers using TCP/IP protocols.

computer.definition: A computer is an electronic device that processes data according to a set of instructions (programs).

algorithm.definition: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure for solving a problem or performing a computation.

artificial intelligence.definition: Artificial intelligence (AI) is the simulation of human intelligence by machines.

machine learning.definition: Machine learning is a subset of AI where systems learn from data without being explicitly programmed.

quantum computing.definition: Quantum computing uses quantum bits (qubits) that can exist in superposition, enabling parallel computation.

pacific ocean.definition: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth, covering about 63 million square miles.

mount everest.definition: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain above sea level at 8,849 meters (29,032 feet).

sahara desert.definition: The Sahara is the world's largest hot desert, covering about 9.2 million square kilometers in North Africa.

amazon river.definition: The Amazon River is the largest river by discharge volume and the second longest river in the world.

great wall of china.definition: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications stretching over 13,000 miles, built to protect against invasions.

world war ii.definition: World War II (1939-1945) was the deadliest conflict in human history, involving most of the world's nations.

roman empire.definition: The Roman Empire (27 BC - 476 AD) was one of the largest and most influential empires in history.

industrial revolution.definition: The Industrial Revolution (1760-1840) was a period of major industrialization that transformed economies and societies.

renaissance.definition: The Renaissance (14th-17th century) was a cultural movement that began in Italy, marking a rebirth of art and learning.

octave.definition: An octave is the interval between one musical pitch and another with double its frequency.

chord.definition: A chord is a group of three or more notes played together in music.

tempo.definition: Tempo is the speed or pace of a piece of music, measured in beats per minute (BPM).

ethics.definition: Ethics is the branch of philosophy that deals with morality and principles of right and wrong behavior.

metaphysics.definition: Metaphysics is the branch of philosophy that examines the fundamental nature of reality.

epistemology.definition: Epistemology is the branch of philosophy concerned with the nature and scope of knowledge.

electron.definition: An electron is a subatomic particle with negative charge (-1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C). Mass: 9.109×10⁻³¹ kg.

proton.definition: A proton is a subatomic particle with positive charge (+1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C). Mass: 1.673×10⁻²⁷ kg.

neutron.definition: A neutron is a subatomic particle with no charge. Mass: 1.675×10⁻²⁷ kg. Found in atomic nucleus.

photon.definition: A photon is a massless boson that carries the electromagnetic force. Speed: c (299,792,458 m/s).

atom.definition: An atom is the basic unit of matter, consisting of a nucleus (protons + neutrons) orbited by electrons.

gravity.definition: Gravity is the fundamental force that attracts objects with mass toward each other. On Earth, g ≈ 9.8 m/s².

universal binary principle.definition: The Universal Binary Principle (UBP) posits that reality is a deterministic, error-corrected projection of a 24-bit substrate using the Golay code and Leech lattice.

molecule.definition: A molecule is a group of two or more atoms bonded together chemically.
